summary.headline: Newgen FY26 revenue rose 6% to INR1,574 crore and Q4 rose 5.3% to INR457 crore, while management declined to guide FY27 growth.
summary.overview: FY26 revenue grew 6% Y-o-Y to INR1,574 crore, with subscription revenue up 24% to INR525 crore and SaaS up 36%. Q4 revenue was INR457 crore against INR430 crore in Q4 FY25, with Q4 SaaS up 44%. Profit after tax was INR301 crore reported, or INR334 crore excluding a one-time Labour Code impact and a INR42 crore legal provision; management described the adjusted PAT as up 6% and the adjusted net margin as 21.3%. Large-deal closures slowed in India, Middle East and EMEA on geopolitical uncertainty and decision delays, and management withheld a FY27 growth number, asking for one more quarter of visibility.

segments.name: U.S.
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 17% Y-o-Y; Q4 U.S. revenue was INR106 crore, up 20% Y-o-Y, driven by insurance journey-led deals and ECM-led banking wins.

segments.name: APAC
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue grew 14% Y-o-Y; management cited strong momentum and newly opened markets in Australia and the U.K., where most deals are subscription.

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue growth muted; license revenue fell more than 20-30% Y-o-Y on lower large-deal wins, while other revenue streams grew. Management said the worst is over.

segments.name: EMEA
segments.commentary: Large-deal closures slowed on West Asia geopolitical uncertainty, especially late in FY26; collections slowed, pushing up trade receivables and DSO.

segments.name: Annuity mix (FY26)
segments.commentary: Of 62% annuity, about 12% is SaaS, 21% is ATS/AMC and about 28% is support.

guidance_outlook: No FY27 revenue or growth number given; management will wait one to two quarters for clarity.
Management said growth in higher teens could bring margin expansion; lower-teens growth would likely keep margins similar.
Company plans 300-400 campus hires in FY27 despite manpower reduction of about 6% Y-o-Y.
Management aims to aggressively reduce trade receivables in FY27.
capex_capacity: Investment in R&D about 8.5% of revenue and sales and marketing about 22% of revenue in FY26.
About 80% of employees have access to AI tools and agents; global headcount approximately 4,300.
Management is exploring inorganic options for go-to-market in mature markets and complementary product technologies; nothing concrete yet.
Filed 12 patents and was granted 2 in FY26; total 67 filings and 25 grants.
demand_pricing: Large-deal momentum slowed across markets; license revenue for India fell more than 20-30%, while total deal count in India and Middle East was almost unchanged.

Notable Q4 wins: Malaysia retail loan origination (RM 6.75 million), Illinois insurer policy binding ($1.6 million), Kuwait bank origination and CCM ($2.2 million), Caribbean insurer NewgenONE ($1.5 million), UAE government tax compliance (AED 5.3 million).
Order book at year-end grew about 13% Y-o-Y.
Customers billing over INR5 crore rose to 101 from 87; 47 new logos added in FY26.
Pricing shifting toward consumption and agentic models; management said pricing is the least headwind.

qa_highlights.question: Is there broader BFSI weakness beyond the Middle East, and what is NBFC demand like in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management saw Middle East disruption only in late Q4 with no long-term weakness; NBFC logo acquisition is growing, with personal finance slow and large public-sector and bank deals delayed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall and is growth or margin guidance available for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Headcount fell about 6% Y-o-Y and manpower was optimized about 7%; management declined to project FY27 growth but said margins may expand if growth reaches higher teens.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 growth band and should double-digit growth be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not give a number and asked for one more quarter; the company expects growth to compound from a smaller license base and from subscription revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did deferred revenue rise from about INR220 crore to about INR300 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to subscription and ATS renewals, plus growth in Australia, the U.K. and U.S., not to a spike in license sales.

qa_highlights.question: What share of revenue is at risk from client AI-driven budget pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the two most exposed streams, about 40% of revenue, could see a 2-3% impact this year.

risks_watch: Large-deal delays in India, Middle East and EMEA; management said the Middle East disruption hit late Q4 and recovery depends on Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Rising trade receivables and slower EMEA and APAC collections, with DSO rising; management says ECL provisioning covers the risk.
Pricing model transition from license to consumption/agentic pricing; management expects clarity in 6-8 months.
Budget pressure on renewals and support, which management estimates at 2-3% impact on about 40% of revenue.
Sustainability of margin: management says margins should hold at lower-teens growth and may expand only if growth reaches higher teens.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term demand: management was confident on product, U.S. and subscription growth but declined to give a FY27 growth figure, citing Middle East disruption and slower large-deal decisions. Management was more confident on cost discipline and cash generation.
key_quotes: So we are slightly focusing on going wide.
In this kind of an environment, projecting a number for next year may not be advisable.
So any time we do any growth, which is lesser than our historical growth, we are quite disappointed.

growth.why: Management declined to give an FY27 revenue growth number, asking for one more quarter of visibility; Q4 revenue grew 5.3% YoY and year-end order book is up about 13%, but no capacity additions or concrete guidance were given.
